diagnosis.proved_by: reading the real shipping sources, then reproducing the symptom with the real provider and the real driver (RED over unchanged 354abd9c0: request_faults=2 reply_faults=0 with the exact native text) and probing the real roster (relist-probe1)
diagnosis.state_is_not_missing: the real roster holds the fixed state for the relisted building through its record (the fixture asserts ROSTER_HOLD == held for the new child key, in-engine, before the expansion); a building listed again with NO LINK holds `never` for the new key, and the real provider refuses its expansion by name
diagnosis.observer_gap: mb_hostplacemap.h place_child_insert -> place_declare sends LINK(sector key, NEW child key), then place_fixed_state states the building under its SECTOR key (it holds one), never under the new city-list key. The host keeps both placements in one record (roster.rs link/merge_fixed). The driver keyed `scan.fixed.held` by the key a report named, so the new child key looked unacknowledged although the host held the record state. Boot (child listed first, sector second) had reported the child key, which is why only the relist failed.
diagnosis.real_c_trace: characterised in the C dialogue check (eech_entity_dialogue_check.c): after a drain and a relist of a sector-placed building the host is asked exactly one LINK (sector key, new child key) and exactly one FIXED_STATE, named by the sector key and not by the new child key
diagnosis.what_was_not_available: no per-request trace of the native run was retained (only the summary row), so the six native requests are inferred from the real C source plus the reproduction, not observed

change.driver: an acknowledged LINK of a LIVE sector placement and a building listed under a city (city.parent) records the pair (scan.fixed.peer); a state acknowledged under a key marks its peer, and a LINK joins whatever state either key already held (scan.fixed.shared). The CityExpand request check asks scan.fixed.holds(child) = acknowledged under that key OR shared through an acknowledged LINK. scan.fixed.held keeps its meaning and its count (fixed_held_lifetime unchanged).
not_done: no blanket acceptance of CityExpand or of a joined count
no acceptance of a valid-looking name
no query-time adoption, second store, API or solver
candidate-lookup joins (scan.fixed.joined, rule-change and withdrawal eligibility) still ask the strict `held`: only the expansion validator changed
row schema and every counter unchanged
strictness_kept: an unlinked key, an unacknowledged or refused LINK, a LINK of an ended or non-live sector key and a state of another record establish nothing
request faults still count before and independently of any UNREACHED classification
